title: WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 -> 1.0 (pure linear LR decay)
description: One constant: WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 -> 1.0, so the LR plateau disappears and lrm = 1 - progress decays linearly to zero from step 0; time-average lrm 0.75 -> 0.50. Nothing else changed (HEAD_DIM 128, DEPTH 10, 2^18 batch, MATRIX_LR 0.04).
reflection: val_bpb 0.989041 vs the 0.988076 baseline: +0.00097, a tie/marginal loss. The comparison is unusually clean - 1120 steps vs 1119, 293.6M tokens vs 293.3M, MFU 42.0% vs 41.9% - so throughput is not a confound and final smoothed train loss (2.759 vs 2.752) agrees with val. All six agents proposed WARMDOWN 0.7 this round; I took 1.0 per a pre-commitment in my proposal so the round would return the shape of the knob instead of a sixth copy of one point. The shape is ASYMMETRIC: 0.3 cost +0.0056 against its matched control, while 1.0 - a 33% cut in the LR integral, much larger than 0.7's 13% - costs ~0.001, i.e. nothing. So the schedule optimum is a broad plateau from ~0.5 upward with a sharp wall below it, and whatever 0.7 scores it can only be a shallow dip between two points that are already equal. The deeper reading is that the 'the run is over-stepped' story from round 2 is wrong as stated: lowering the *global* LR integral by a third does essentially nothing, so the round-2 MATRIX_LR regressions were about Muon's step size relative to the Adam groups (the ratio), not about total LR magnitude. Schedule axis: closed. Still untouched after 18 runs: WINDOW_PATTERN, EMBEDDING_LR/UNEMBEDDING_LR, ADAM_BETAS, WEIGHT_DECAY, the MLP 4x ratio, and MATRIX_LR DOWN (0.03), which is the one direction the ratio reading actually points at.
